sprite.note: Inject a sprite into the document ONCE, then reference symbols by hash. This is how the 39 house glyphs already work.

mask.note: For a single glyph, or where CSS must own the glyph (pseudo-elements, backgrounds). Tints via background:currentColor, so ink still inherits.

antipattern.why: Cross-document <use> is SVG 2 and was never shipped in Blink or WebKit. It renders nothing in Chrome, Edge, and Safari — only Firefox resolves it. Inject the sprite first, or use the mask pattern.

classes.ico: wears a <use> glyph — sets size token + fill:currentColor
classes.ico-mask: wears a loose SVG as a CSS mask — background:currentColor does the tinting

inkTokens.--toc-icon-ink: currentColor — the default; the glyph takes the ink of its context
inkTokens.--toc-icon-ink-thread: var(--toc-gold-700) — the AA-safe gold for glyphs on light ground
inkTokens.--toc-icon-ink-onDark: var(--toc-ivory) — glyphs on violet / sage / blue grounds

rules: Resolve meaning through `semantic` first; reach into `icons` only when no semantic token fits.
Never reference a sprite across documents — inject it, then use the hash. See `antipattern`.
One weight sitewide — `regular`. Mixing weights breaks the vocabulary.
Never hardcode a pixel size; use a size token or its ico-* class.
Never set fill/stroke on the glyph; let currentColor inherit the surface ink.
Sacred Gold #B8965A fails AA as ink — use --toc-icon-ink-thread (gold-700) for gold glyphs on light.
The 39 house glyphs (#icon-*) are the bespoke layer and outrank the pack where both exist.
Only four custom icons are sanctioned for core pages; everything else comes from this pack.
